Extract muscle force directions from an OpenSim model

Source: R/muscle_force_direction.R
muscle_force_direction.Rd

Calculates anatomical and/or effective muscle attachment locations and normalised muscle force-direction vectors for selected physical frames in an OpenSim musculoskeletal model.

Usage

muscle_force_direction(
  model_file = "model.osim",
  kinematics_file = NULL,
  target_frame_names = "femur_r",
  output_frame_name = "femur_r",
  line_of_action_mode = "effective",
  selected_muscle_names = NULL,
  file_output = "muscle_force_directions.csv",
  kinematics_in_degrees = TRUE,
  strict_kinematics_columns = FALSE,
  equilibrate_muscles = FALSE,
  print_progress = TRUE,
  write_file = T,
  return_object = F
)

Arguments

model_file

A character string giving the path to an OpenSim model file, normally with extension .osim. The file must exist and be readable by the OpenSim Python package.

kinematics_file

Either a character string giving the path to an OpenSim motion or states file, normally with extension .mot or .sto, or `NULL`. When a file is supplied, the function evaluates the muscle paths at every kinematic frame in that file. When `NULL`, the model is evaluated once using the default coordinate values established by `Model$initSystem()`.

target_frame_names

A character vector containing the names of the bodies or physical frames on which the muscle forces act. Body names such as `"femur_r"` may be supplied directly. Use `"ground"` for the OpenSim ground frame. An absolute OpenSim component path may be used for a physical frame that is not directly accessible by body name.

Each returned force vector points away from its attachment on the target frame and toward the remainder of the muscle path.

output_frame_name

A single character string specifying the reference frame in which attachment coordinates, force-direction vectors, and transport moments are expressed. Use `"ground"` to return global coordinates, a body name such as `"femur_r"` to return body-local coordinates, or an absolute OpenSim component path for another physical frame.

line_of_action_mode

A single character string specifying which attachment definition to return. Must be one of:

`"anatomical"`

Return the terminal anatomical attachment and the direction from that attachment toward the immediately adjacent point in the evaluated muscle path.

`"effective"`

Return the effective attachment at the boundary of the group of current path points attached to the target frame, together with the direction toward the first path point outside that frame.

`"both"`

Return separate anatomical and effective rows for each eligible muscle, target frame, and kinematic frame.

selected_muscle_names

Either `NULL` or a character vector containing exact OpenSim muscle names, for example `c("addlong_r", "semiten_r")`. When `NULL`, all muscles in the model are inspected. Muscle names must match the names stored in `model$getMuscles()`.

file_output

A character string giving the path of the CSV file to create when `write_file = TRUE`. Parent directories are not created automatically unless this is explicitly implemented in the function. The argument is ignored when `write_file = FALSE`.

kinematics_in_degrees

A logical value or `NA`.

* `TRUE` indicates that rotational-coordinate values in `kinematics_file` are expressed in degrees and must be converted to radians before being assigned to the OpenSim state. * `FALSE` indicates that rotational-coordinate values are already in radians. * `NA` instructs the function to inspect the `inDegrees` metadata field in the OpenSim table. If that metadata is absent, the implementation should fall back to radians.

Translational coordinates are not converted.

strict_kinematics_columns

Logical. If `FALSE`, columns in the kinematics file that cannot be matched to model coordinates are ignored. If `TRUE`, the function stops when it encounters an unmatched, non-speed column. Columns ending in `"/speed"` are ignored because the muscle-path calculation requires only Position-stage model realisation.

equilibrate_muscles

Logical. If `TRUE`, `model$equilibrateMuscles(state)` is called after applying each kinematic frame. Muscle equilibration is generally unnecessary when only attachment positions and force directions are required, and may fail for physiologically or numerically problematic states. The default is `FALSE`.

print_progress

Logical. If `TRUE`, print progress messages while processing kinematic frames and report muscles skipped because their topology is not handled by the MATLAB-equivalent selection logic.

write_file

Logical. If `TRUE`, write the resulting data frame to the CSV path specified by `file_output`. If `FALSE`, no output file is created.

return_object

Logical. If `TRUE`, return the result as an R data frame. If `FALSE`, return the result invisibly. Setting both `write_file = FALSE` and `return_object = FALSE` performs the analysis without providing a readily accessible result and is therefore usually not useful.

Value

When `return_object = TRUE`, a data frame containing one row for each eligible combination of kinematic frame, muscle, target frame, and requested line-of-action mode. When `return_object = FALSE`, the same data frame is returned invisibly.

Depending on the implemented options, columns include:

`time`

Time corresponding to the evaluated model state.

`muscle`

OpenSim muscle name.

`target_frame`

Component path of the frame on which the force acts.

`output_frame`

Component path of the frame used to express results.

`mode`

Either `"anatomical"` or `"effective"`.

`side`

Whether the vector points toward the start or end of the ordered muscle path.

`attachment_point`

Name of the selected attachment path point.

`adjacent_point`

Name of the path point used to define direction.

`point_x`, `point_y`, `point_z`

Attachment coordinates expressed in `output_frame_name`, normally in metres.

`direction_x`, `direction_y`, `direction_z`

Components of the normalised force-direction vector expressed in `output_frame_name`.

`transport_moment_x`, `transport_moment_y`, `transport_moment_z`

Transport-moment components associated with relocating the effective unit force from the effective attachment to the anatomical attachment. These have dimensions of length until multiplied by a force magnitude. Anatomical rows contain zero.

Details

The function accesses the OpenSim Python API through reticulate. For each model state, it evaluates the current muscle geometry path and reproduces the attachment-selection logic used by the the MuscleForceDirection tool (https://github.com/modenaxe/MuscleForceDirection/tree/master).

Anatomical force directions are calculated at the terminal anatomical attachment of the muscle on the target frame. Effective force directions are calculated at the boundary point where the current muscle path enters or leaves the target frame.

All returned force-direction vectors point from the selected target frame outward into the remainder of the muscle path. Direction vectors are normalised to unit length.

The function requires a Python environment containing a compatible installation of the `opensim` Python module. It does not install OpenSim or select a Python or Conda environment automatically.

Users should configure reticulate before calling the function, for example with `reticulate::use_condaenv()` or `reticulate::use_python()`. Python selection normally must occur before Python is initialised in the current R session. reticulate supports selecting Python, virtual environments, and Conda environments.

Both anatomical and effective results are derived from the same evaluated current muscle path. The implementation assumes that muscle path points are ordered from proximal to distal, matching the MATLAB MuscleForceDirection implementation.

A muscle is skipped for a target frame when neither its first nor final current path point is attached to that frame, even if intermediate via points are attached to it. A muscle that both starts and ends on the same target frame is also skipped because this topology is not defined by the MATLAB implementation.

Attachment coordinates are points, whereas force directions are free vectors. To avoid applying translation to a direction vector, the function transforms the attachment and adjacent point into the requested output frame, subtracts the transformed points, and then normalises the resulting vector.

The returned direction components do not represent a second point. To create an arrow endpoint of length `L`, calculate:

“` end_x <- point_x + L * direction_x end_y <- point_y + L * direction_y end_z <- point_z + L * direction_z “`

Python requirements

The selected Python environment must contain the `opensim` module. The function imports that module with `reticulate::import()`. The reticulate import interface makes a Python module available as an R object whose attributes and methods can be accessed with `$`.

Coordinate units

OpenSim models conventionally represent distances in metres and rotational coordinates internally in radians. The function converts rotational kinematics from degrees when `kinematics_in_degrees = TRUE`.

Direction vectors are dimensionless. The transport-moment output calculated from a unit force direction and an attachment displacement has dimensions of length. Multiplying it by a muscle force in newtons produces a moment in newton-metres.
